title: Aalsterse vla (Aalst spiced bread pudding tart)

ingredients.name: stale soft aniseed bread (mastel) or milk rolls

steps: Heat the oven to 180 degrees C. Roll out the pastry and line a 24 cm tart tin.
Tear the bread into pieces and soak it in the milk for 20 minutes until completely soft.
Crumble the speculoos or gingerbread and stir it into the bread mixture, mashing with a fork to make a thick paste.
Beat in the sugar, syrup, eggs, cinnamon and cloves until combined.
Pour the mixture into the pastry case and level the top.
Bake for about 45 minutes until the filling is firm, dark and slightly caramelised at the edges. Cool before slicing.

title: Babelutte (honey and brown sugar toffee from Veurne)
steps: Butter a shallow tray or line it with baking paper.
Put the sugar, honey, butter, cream and salt in a heavy saucepan and heat gently, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved.
Raise the heat to medium and let the mixture bubble without stirring too much until it reaches about 140 degrees C on a sugar thermometer.
Pour the toffee onto the prepared tray and let it cool for a few minutes until it begins to firm.
Score it into small squares with a knife while still warm.
Once fully hard, break along the lines and wrap each piece in paper. Store in an airtight tin.

title: Belgian waffle (light yeast-raised Brussels-style waffle)

ingredients.name: icing sugar, whipped cream and strawberries

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk in the warm milk, egg yolks, melted butter and vanilla to make a smooth batter. Cover and leave for about 45 minutes until bubbly.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks in a clean bowl and fold them gently into the batter so it stays airy.
Heat a waffle iron and brush it lightly with butter or oil.
Pour in enough batter to fill the grid and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until crisp and golden.
Serve hot, dusted with icing sugar and topped with whipped cream and strawberries.

title: Boûkète (Liège buckwheat pancake with raisins)
steps: Mix both flours with the yeast and salt, then whisk in the warm milk and egg until you have a thick, smooth batter.
Stir in the raisins, cover the bowl and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour until bubbly.
Heat a spoonful of lard or butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Pour in a small ladleful of batter to make a pancake about 1 cm thick and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the underside is dark golden.
Flip and cook the second side for 2 to 3 minutes. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve hot, sprinkled with brown sugar or drizzled with syrup.

title: Cougnou (Christmas sweet bread shaped like the infant Jesus)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the milk, egg and yolk and knead until you have a soft dough.
Knead in the butter and continue for about 10 minutes until smooth. Work in the raisins if using.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for about 1 hour.
Shape the dough into two elongated ovals, pinching one end of each slightly to suggest a head, or into one large oval, and place them on a lined tray.
Let the shaped loaves rise for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 190 degrees C.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with pearl sugar and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.

title: Craquelin (Belgian sweet brioche bun with sugar nibs)

ingredients.name: pearl sugar or crushed sugar cubes

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the milk and 2 eggs and knead to a soft dough.
Work in the butter a little at a time and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and silky.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces and shape into balls or short ovals. Place on a lined tray and let rise again for 40 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C. Brush the buns with beaten egg and press a generous amount of pearl sugar on top.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden, then cool on a rack.

title: Croquettes aux crevettes (grey shrimp croquettes)

ingredients.name: warm milk (or half milk and half fish stock)
peeled small cooked shrimp (grey shrimp if available)

steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the 40 g of flour and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Whisk in the warm milk a little at a time to make a very thick, smooth béchamel, stirring until it pulls cleanly from the sides of the pan.
Fold in the shrimp, parsley and nutmeg and season well. Spread the mixture on a plate, cover and chill for at least 3 hours until completely firm.
Shape the cold mixture into 8 cylinders or balls with floured hands.
Roll each one in flour, then in beaten egg, then in breadcrumbs. For a sturdier crust, dip in egg and crumbs a second time.
Heat the oil to 175 degrees C and fry the croquettes in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden brown and hot in the middle.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Gaufre de Liège (Liège waffle with caramelised pearl sugar)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the warm milk, eggs and vanilla and knead until a smooth, sticky dough forms.
Work in the soft butter a piece at a time and keep kneading for about 10 minutes until the dough is soft and elastic.
Cover and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Gently knead in the pearl sugar, then divide the dough into 6 balls and let them rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a waffle iron, ideally with deep pockets. Cook each ball for 3 to 4 minutes until the waffle is dark golden and the sugar has caramelised.
Let them cool for a minute on a rack, as the sugar is extremely hot, and eat warm, plain.

title: Mitraillette (baguette stuffed with meat, fries and sauce)

ingredients.name: baguettes, each cut in half crosswise
beef burger patties, or 4 thin steaks

steps: Split the baguette pieces lengthwise and toast the cut sides briefly under a grill.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the patties for about 4 minutes per side until cooked through. Season with salt.
Cook the fries until golden and crisp, or reheat leftover fries in a hot oven.
Spread the bread with the mayonnaise and the sauce.
Layer in lettuce, tomato, onion and a patty, then pile a handful of fries on each and close the sandwich.
Serve at once with extra sauce.

title: Moules-frites (steamed mussels with fries)
steps: Scrub the mussels under cold water, pull off any beards, and throw away any that stay open when tapped or have cracked shells.
Cut the potatoes into thick sticks, rinse them and dry them thoroughly. Heat the oil to 150 degrees C and fry the potatoes in batches for about 6 minutes until soft but not coloured. Drain.
Melt the butter in a very large pot and soften the onion and celery for 4 to 5 minutes without browning.
Add the wine and bay leaf and bring to a boil. Tip in the mussels, cover tightly and cook over high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until the shells open.
Meanwhile raise the oil to 180 degrees C and fry the potatoes a second time for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain and salt generously.
Discard any mussels that stayed shut. Sprinkle the parsley and pepper over the mussels and serve them in the pot with the cooking juices, with the fries and mayonnaise on the side.

title: Pain à la grecque (Brussels flat cinnamon-sugar bread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk and melted butter and knead into a smooth dough. Cover and let it rise for about 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 220 degrees C. Roll the dough out very thinly into a large rectangle and cut it into four smaller rectangles.
Brush each lightly with water.
Mix the brown sugar with the cinnamon and press it firmly into the dough so it sticks.
Sprinkle the granulated sugar over the top and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the dough is crisp and the sugar is caramelised and bubbling.
Cool for a few minutes so the caramel sets, then break into pieces and eat the same day.

title: Paling in 't groen (eel in green herb sauce)

ingredients.name: eel, skinned or skin-on, cleaned and cut into 5 cm pieces (ask the fishmonger)
mixed fresh herbs such as sorrel, spinach, parsley, chervil, tarragon and mint, chopped

steps: Rinse the eel pieces and pat them dry.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and soften the shallots gently without colouring them.
Add the eel, wine and stock and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook very gently for about 15 minutes until the flesh pulls easily from the bone. The eel must be fully cooked through.
Add the chopped herbs and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes more until wilted but still bright green.
Take the pan off the heat. Mix the egg yolks with a ladleful of the hot liquid, then stir this back into the pan so the sauce thickens slightly. Do not let it boil again or it may curdle.
Add the lemon juice, season with salt and white pepper and serve warm or cold with bread or potatoes.

title: Pistolet (Belgian crusty bread roll)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl, then add the water and oil and knead for about 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let the dough rise for about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 equal pieces and shape each into a ball. Cover and rest for 10 minutes.
Flatten each ball slightly and press a deep crease through the middle with the side of your hand or a thin rolling pin, then fold the dough over itself along the crease.
Place the rolls on a floured tray, cover and let them rise for 30 to 40 minutes.
Heat the oven to 230 degrees C with a tray of water on the bottom shelf to make steam. Dust the rolls with flour and bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden with a crisp crust.

title: Sauce andalouse (Belgian tomato and pepper mayonnaise)

ingredients.name: finely chopped roasted red pepper (from a jar)

steps: Put the mayonnaise in a bowl.
Stir in the tomato paste until evenly blended and the colour is a uniform orange.
Chop the roasted pepper as finely as you can and fold it in along with the lemon juice, paprika and sugar.
Taste and adjust, adding more paprika or lemon if needed.
Chill for 30 minutes so the flavours blend, then serve with fries, burgers or fried snacks.

title: Steak frites (pan-fried steak with fries)

ingredients.name: sirloin or rump steaks, about 200 g each

steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and pat them dry.
Cut the potatoes into thick sticks, rinse and dry them. Fry them in oil at 150 degrees C for about 6 minutes until tender but pale, then drain.
Season the steaks generously with salt and pepper. Heat the tablespoon of oil in a heavy frying pan over high heat until it just starts to smoke.
Sear the steaks for 2 to 3 minutes per side for medium-rare, adding the butter, garlic and thyme for the last minute and spooning the foaming butter over the meat.
Rest the steaks on a warm plate for 5 minutes.
Reheat the oil to 180 degrees C and fry the potatoes a second time for about 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain, salt and serve beside the steaks with mayonnaise.

title: Tarte al d'jote (Nivelles chard and fresh cheese tart)

ingredients.name: soft fresh cheese with herbs, such as boulette de Nivelles, or garlic-and-herb cream cheese

steps: Heat the oven to 190 degrees C. Roll out the pastry and line a 24 cm tart tin, then prick the base and chill while you prepare the filling.
Blanch the chard leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain, cool and squeeze out as much water as possible. Chop finely.
Fry the chard in the butter for 3 minutes to dry it out further and let it cool a little.
Beat the soft cheese with the eggs and cream until smooth and season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Stir in the chard, spread the mixture in the pastry case and level the top.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the filling is set and golden. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Zoervleis (Limburg sweet-and-sour beef stew)

ingredients.name: stewing beef, cut into 3 cm cubes
gingerbread or spiced rye cake, crumbled

steps: Combine the vinegar, water and bay leaves and pour over the beef. Marinate in the fridge for at least 3 hours.
Lift the meat from the marinade, pat dry and keep the marinade to one side.
Melt the butter in a heavy casserole and brown the beef in batches. Remove each batch to a plate.
Soften the onions in the same pot for 8 minutes until golden, then return the beef.
Add the stock and about half the strained marinade, then stir in the crumbled gingerbread, apple syrup and mustard.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours until the beef is tender and the sauce is thick, dark and gently sweet-sour. Taste and season, adding a little more marinade if you want more tang.
Serve with boiled potatoes or fries.
